question: Should OpenClaw accept static SecretRefs resolving into `sandbox.docker.env` values that are passed to Docker as inspectable container environment variables?
rationale: The implementation is feasible and has an open PR, but the remaining choice is a maintainer/security boundary decision about credential delivery into Docker env metadata, not a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Accept and land the linked PR
options.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98216 after recording that static SecretRefs may resolve into Docker env values with the existing metadata warning.

options.title: Require stronger warning or gating
options.body: Ask the PR to make the Docker metadata exposure more explicit in docs or operator-facing output before merge.

options.title: Reject env-based secret delivery
options.body: Close or redirect the implementation toward a non-env secret delivery design if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable for SecretRef-backed values.

recommendation.title: Accept and land the linked PR
recommendation.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98216 after recording that static SecretRefs may resolve into Docker env values with the existing metadata warning.
